comment_content:
I would back Srivatsan Srinivasan. Super impressive project should make
business sense. And to be more clear, it should be prescriptive. Recently we
worked on Absenteeism in employees and we found that posture of working is
impacting health and also having a pet reduces stress - it took more than 6
hours to arrive it this conclusion. So these inputs can be given to HR - which
makes more sense instead of pitching to HR that given an employee, I can tell
how many hours he will be absent. This can happen with better EDA. Next, I
would like projects which has modelling taken progressively from simple
logistic to Random Forest instead of Deep Learning directly. And the projects
which verify assumptions of models and apply them rather than randomly trying
each of them makes more sense.For example, a linear regression applied after
verifying homoscedasticity or making SVM robust enough just because business
doesn't allow outliers to be removed. etc. For me a project which gives me a
ton of insights is the best one. And as usual, cause oriented, AI for good
with neat, clean and self explanatory code, !! (edited)
